name: Audio input token count explodes relative to text output
workarounds: Use 30-second windowing (Whisper's max_source_positions=1500 at 50Hz mel frame rate)
Use VAD to skip non-speech segments
Use streaming ASR for long audio (with quality tradeoff)
notes: A 1-hour recording at 16kHz is 57,600,000 samples. After the log-mel frontend (80 or 128 mel bins, 100Hz frame rate for Whisper), this becomes 360,000 mel frames. Whisper's encoder uses 30-second windowing (max_source_positions=1500 at 50Hz after 2x subsampling), so a 1-hour recording is processed as 120 separate 30-second windows. Each window produces 1,500 encoder positions. The encoder is bidirectional with full attention, so the compute cost per window is O(1500^2 * d_model * num_layers). For large-v3 (d_model=1280, 32 layers), this is approximately 1500^2 * 1280 * 32 * 2 * 2 = 368 GFLOP per window, or 44 TFLOP for the full hour. The decoder then generates text tokens autoregressively, but the encoder dominates the compute. This is fundamentally different from text-to-text models where input and output token counts are comparable.
